newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - DEC 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - DEC 13.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--In a bid to impress upon the public the seriousness of its battle against tax evasion, the finance ministry yesterday released a list of persons and companies accused of major tax evasion. Embarrassingly, two subsidiaries of state-run banks are also on the list.
--Agriculture Minister Stephanos Tzoumakas lashes out at cotton farmers in the Thessaly region, allegedly calling them 'mafiosi'.
--A new study by ICAP says industry will continue to improve in 1997 with most industries saying they expect an increase in the volume of sales.
--Inflation and reduced wages are considered by Greek households to be the major reasons for a drop in living standards, the ICAP survey adds.
IMERISIA
--Representatives of business yesterday made an appeal to government and farmers to find a solution to their differences before it was too late for the economy.
--Eight in 10 Greek households expected a drop in economic standing during 1997, adversely affecting their consumer power, the ICAP survey says.
--Hellenic Bottling company 3E will undertake the bottling of Coca-Cola in Nigeria as the company renews its contract with Coca-Cola for another 10 years.
KERDOS
--Businessmen protest over the publication of the list of tax evaders, saying a number of cases were being resolved, or not of the same magnitude as the others.

--The national economy ministry has sounded the alarm over the course of inflation for December, following the farmers' protests. Adverse repercussions also expected for interest rates and the public debt if the blockade is not resolved quickly.

--Hatzioannou Brothers yesterday submitted a bid fgor the Hliofin AE company, sources said. The Group is involved in the production of women's hosiery and is known for its ownership of the Xanthi casino.
--Eurobank and Interbank will operate jointly in 1997, sources say, becoming the third largest private bank in the Greek market.
EXPRESS

--Signs of fatigue at the blockades as it enters its 16th day. Farmers squabble over whether to stay or go or to abandon blockades as a form of pressure altogether. The number of road blocks meanwhile has been reduced but the existing blocks are being reinforced.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--The Federation of Greek Industries yesterday disputed the ICAP report on business activity, saying the picture was not as rosy as it was being painted.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
